name: Luxembourg
tagline: One small multilingual university, and a semester abroad built in
summary: Luxembourg has essentially one public university, founded in 2003, and it is unlike anywhere else on this site. Programmes are multilingual by design - many bachelor's are taught in two languages, typically French and English or French and German - and every bachelor student has to spend a semester abroad, which is written into the rules rather than offered as an option. It is small, well funded, and sits at the centre of EU institutions and international finance. The country is also one of the most expensive in Europe to live in, and there is only one annual intake, in September.
whyConsider: Very low public tuition compared with anywhere outside continental Europe, and the same fee whether you are EU or not.
A compulsory semester abroad in every bachelor's degree, so international mobility is guaranteed rather than something you have to organise.
Multilingualism is the point: if you have IB French B or German B alongside English, Luxembourg turns that into an asset rather than a hurdle.
Small cohorts and close contact with staff at a university of a few thousand students.
Location. The Court of Justice of the EU, the European Investment Bank, Eurostat and a large financial sector are all in the same city, which matters for law, economics and finance internships.
watchOuts: English alone is often not enough. Many bachelor's require French or German as well as English, and the requirement is per programme. Read the language requirements of the individual programme before anything else.

One intake a year, in September, with no spring or summer entry. Applications for 2027-2028 open on 1 February 2027, and the university has said the admission criteria for that year are under review and may change.
Very small choice. This is one university with a limited range of bachelor's - if your subject is not among them, Luxembourg is simply not an option.
Cost of living is high. Rents in and around Luxembourg City are among the most expensive in the EU, and student housing is limited.
The compulsory mobility semester is a real constraint if you have family or work commitments; waivers exist but are not automatic.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University of Luxembourg assesses foreign school-leaving diplomas individually against its programme-specific admission criteria, and states that the criteria for 2027-2028 are under review. No published IB-specific rule was found on an official page during this research. The decisive requirement in practice is the language combination the programme demands, not a points threshold.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No official IB-to-Luxembourgish conversion was found during this research.
notes: A full IB Diploma is a university-entrance qualification recognised across the EU, and Luxembourg admits students from a very wide range of national systems - but confirm your specific case with the university's student department (SEVE) rather than assuming.
If you plan to have your degree formally recognised in Luxembourg later, Luxembourg maintains a Register of Titles (registre des titres) for higher education qualifications.
Because the admission criteria for 2027-2028 were still being revised when this file was written, treat everything here as provisional and re-read the university's admissions pages in late 2026.

deadlines.label: Applications open for the 2027-2028 academic year
deadlines.year: 2027-2028 entry - stated on the university's own admissions page
deadlines.notes: The university offers only one annual intake for bachelor's and master's, in September. The closing date for 2027-2028 was not published at the time of research, and the university warns that the admission criteria for that year are under review and may change.

deadlines.label: Closing date for bachelor applications
deadlines.notes: For the 2026-2027 cycle the application period had already closed by September 2026. Luxembourg's public service portal describes enrolment as running from the end of April to mid-September but notes that enrolment periods for some bachelor programmes are subject to change and that its own page is being updated. Check uni.lu from February 2027.

steps: Choose a programme from the university's bachelor list and read its language requirements first - this is what decides whether Luxembourg is viable for you.
Check the eligibility criteria for that programme, and note that the criteria for 2027-2028 were under review when this was written.
Prepare your documents: IB transcript or predicted grades, school-leaving certificate, proof of the required languages, passport, motivation letter.
Create an account on the university's admission platform when applications open on 1 February 2027.
Complete the application and pay the application fee, then submit online.
If admitted, enrol and pay the semester registration fee, and start looking for accommodation immediately - housing is the tightest constraint in Luxembourg.
Plan for the compulsory semester abroad, normally taken in the third, fourth or fifth semester.
application.selectionNotes: Admission is decided by the university programme by programme against published eligibility criteria, rather than by a national points system or a central office. There is no numerus fixus system of the Dutch kind and no CAO-style ranking; the practical filters are the language combination and the subject prerequisites of the individual programme.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Small and mostly multilingual rather than purely English. The University of Luxembourg builds bachelor's around combinations of French, English and German, so a programme described as partly English-taught may still require French or German for a substantial part of the teaching. A few programmes are taught wholly in English. No verified count of fully English-taught bachelor programmes was found during this research.
language.englishProof: Set per programme by the University of Luxembourg; no national rule. An IB Diploma taken in English will usually satisfy the English component, but you must check whether the programme also requires French or German and at what level.
notes: Luxembourgish is the national language, with French and German as administrative languages. You will not normally need Luxembourgish to study, but French is genuinely useful for daily life, administration and student jobs.
If you took French B or German B in the IB, say so in your application - the multilingual profile is exactly what this university is built around.
Luxembourg also runs BTS programmes (two-year higher technician diplomas) in its secondary schools, taught mainly in French; these are a different route from a university bachelor's.

The University of Luxembourg's fee pages could not be retrieved during this research - uni.lu returned CloudFront 403 errors and the Luxembourg public service page for enrolling at the university states that it is currently being updated. All fee fields are therefore left empty rather than guessed.

Registration fees at the University of Luxembourg are charged per semester rather than per year, and are widely reported as being higher in the first year than in later years, with the same amount for EU and non-EU students. These figures were NOT confirmed on an official page and must be verified at uni.lu before you rely on them.
There is an application fee per application, which is reported to be deducted from your first semester fee if you enrol - again, verify this at uni.lu.

Luxembourg has one of the highest costs of living in the EU, driven mainly by rent. Budget well above what you would need in Belgium or the Netherlands, and check the university's own cost-of-living page.

funding: Danish SU taken abroad is the realistic backbone of your funding - apply to Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen before you leave.

Luxembourg state financial aid for higher education (AideFi, the successor to CEDIES aid) exists in the form of grants and loans, and is administered through guichet.public.lu. It is aimed at residents and at the children of people working in Luxembourg; the exact eligibility conditions for a newly arrived EU student were not verified during this research, so check them at guichet.public.lu before assuming you qualify.
Erasmus+ funding is available for the compulsory mobility semester, which reduces its cost.
Student jobs exist in Luxembourg City and pay comparatively well, but often expect French and sometimes Luxembourgish.
workRights: As an EU citizen you may work in Luxembourg without a permit. Luxembourg publishes specific rules for combining studies and paid work at guichet.public.lu under 'Working and studying', including rules on student contracts during school holidays. The current hour limits and student-contract conditions were not verified during this research - check https://guichet.public.lu/en/citoyens/famille-education/etudes-superieures/activite-professionnelle.html before you take a job.
residency: As an EU citizen you enter with your Danish passport or ID card and need no visa. You must make a declaration of arrival at the commune where you live, and after three months register as an EU citizen residing in Luxembourg, showing proof of enrolment, sufficient resources and health cover. Non-EU students need a temporary authorisation to stay before travelling, followed by a residence permit after arrival.
housing: The hardest practical problem of studying in Luxembourg. The country has one of the most expensive rental markets in the EU and the student population competes with a large professional and cross-border workforce. The University of Luxembourg runs its own student housing service and this should be your first and main approach - apply as soon as you are admitted, not after. If you miss university housing, consider living just across the border in France, Germany or Belgium and commuting: public transport inside Luxembourg is free, and many students in the Greater Region do exactly this. No official rent figures were verified for this file.
healthcare: Bring your European Health Insurance Card from Denmark. If you register as a resident and study in Luxembourg for a full degree, you will normally be affiliated to the Luxembourg health insurance system (CNS) - the university's student department explains the process during enrolment. Non-EU students must show proof of health cover to obtain their residence permit.

institutions.name: University of Luxembourg
institutions.englishBachelors: A small multilingual bachelor portfolio; several programmes involve English alongside French or German
institutions.note: The country's only public university, built on a redeveloped steelworks site at Belval, with a compulsory semester abroad in every bachelor's degree.

institutions.name: LUNEX University
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught bachelor's in physiotherapy, sport and exercise science and health management
institutions.note: A private, fully English-taught health and sport university - the most straightforward English-language bachelor route in Luxembourg, but it charges private tuition.

institutions.name: Sacred Heart University Luxembourg
institutions.englishBachelors: Primarily a graduate business school; check whether any undergraduate provision applies to you
institutions.note: The Luxembourg campus of an American university, teaching in English and focused on business; verify its current undergraduate offer directly, as the provision is mainly at master's level.

institutions.name: Miami University John E. Dolibois European Center
institutions.englishBachelors: Study-abroad provision for Miami University students rather than a standalone degree route
institutions.note: An American university campus in a Luxembourg chateau; included for completeness - it is a study-abroad centre, not a normal entry point for a Danish IB student.

institutions.name: BBI - Luxembourg Hotel and Tourism Management School
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught hospitality and tourism management bachelor's
institutions.note: A small private hospitality school in the north of the country teaching in English, with placements built into the programme; confirm accreditation and fees directly.
